title: Smooth labelled isomorphism fibres of a forgetful tower
statement:
Let $k$ be a field, $g\geq2$ and $n\geq0$ integers. Use the stable ordered pointed moduli groupoids of [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids] and their forgetful-and-stabilizing maps $F_r:\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,r+1}\to\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,r}$. Suppose given $k$-schemes $T_r$ and maps $a_r:T_r\to\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,r}$, for $0\leq r\leq n$, and maps $q_r:T_{r+1}\to T_r$, for $r<n$, with specified 2-cartesian squares $a_rq_r\simeq F_ra_{r+1}$. Denote the corresponding stable families by $(X_r\to T_r,s_{1,r},\ldots,s_{r,r})$ and put $q=q_0\circ\cdots\circ q_{n-1}:T_n\to T_0$ (the identity for $n=0$).

Let $F/k$ be any field extension and $C/F$ a smooth projective geometrically connected genus-$g$ curve with ordered distinct $F$-rational points $p_1,\ldots,p_n$. For an $F$-scheme $B$, put $C_B=C\times_F B$. There is a bijection, natural under pullback in $B$, between the set of pairs $(m,\alpha)$ with $m:B\to T_n$ a $k$-map and $\alpha:(X_n\times_{T_n}B,s_{1,n,B},\ldots,s_{n,n,B})\xrightarrow{\sim}(C_B,p_{1,B},\ldots,p_{n,B})$ an isomorphism preserving every label, and the set of pairs $(m_0,\beta)$ with $m_0:B\to T_0$ a $k$-map and $\beta:X_0\times_{T_0}B\xrightarrow{\sim}C_B$ an unpointed $B$-isomorphism. The first coordinate on the second side is $m_0=q\circ m$; $\beta$ is the isomorphism induced by forgetting all markings and stabilizing, using the specified squares. The inverse has marking sections $\beta^{-1}\circ p_{i,B}$ under these identifications. These are sets of actual morphism-and-isomorphism pairs; no quotient by $\operatorname{Aut}(C_B)$ or by permutations is taken.

Fields, field extensions, schemes, smoothness, projectivity and fibre products use [def-weil-field], [def-pc-field-extension], [def-pc-scheme], [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], [def-kun-projective] and [def-pc-fibre-product]. Genus, labelled stable families, 2-fibre products and forgetting/stabilizing have the meanings fixed above and in [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids] and [lem-sfb-knudsen-pointed-forgetful-universal-curve].

proof.text: Write $\chi_r(m):a_r(q_rm)\xrightarrow{\sim}F_r(a_{r+1}(m))$ for the specified comparison. Unpack one 2-cartesian square over $B$: its comparison functor sends $m:B\to T_{r+1}$ to $(q_rm,a_{r+1}(m),\chi_r(m))$ and is an equivalence with the groupoid of triples $(b,Y,\theta:a_r(b)\xrightarrow{\sim}F_rY)$. For a fixed triple, essential surjectivity gives an isomorphism from a comparison object to it. The first component is in the discrete groupoid $h_{T_r}(B)$, so it forces $q_rm=b$; its second component is an isomorphism $\gamma:a_{r+1}(m)\xrightarrow{\sim}Y$ with $F_r(\gamma)\chi_r(m)=\theta$. Two such choices give, by full faithfulness, an arrow between their maps in $h_{T_{r+1}}(B)$. Since this is the discrete representable groupoid, the maps are equal and that arrow is the identity; its image forces the two $\gamma$ to agree. This argument keeps the comparison $\theta$ fixed, so no automorphism of the target family is discarded. Thus this is a unique actual pair $(m,\gamma)$, not just an isomorphism class. This is the definition of 2-cartesianness applied to the explicit groupoids in the cited definition.

source.place: Section 2, Corollary 2.6 and smooth disjoint-section case; agent assembly from the cited universal-curve statement and the specified 2-cartesian squares. Local PDF WANTED.

proof.text: For $(m_n,\alpha_n)$ on the pointed side, set $m_r=q_r\cdots q_{n-1}m_n$. Starting at $r=n-1$, define $\alpha_r=\delta_r F_r(\alpha_{r+1})\chi_r(m_{r+1})$, where $\delta_r:F_r(C_B,p_{1,B},\ldots,p_{r+1,B})\xrightarrow{\sim}(C_B,p_{1,B},\ldots,p_{r,B})$ is the canonical forgetting identification. The target is $(C_B,p_{1,B},\ldots,p_{r,B})$: the cited smooth-locus clause says forgetting a disjoint last marking leaves the underlying smooth curve unchanged. Each stage is a stable family because it is the image under $F_r$, and the same clause identifies its target with this truncation. Thus the recursion is defined all the way down, and gives $(m_0,\beta)=(q m_n,\alpha_0)$. For $n=0$ it gives the original pair. Smoothness and disjointness needed here hold for the fixed smooth curve and its distinct sections after pullback to $B$; this is the smooth disjoint-section case under arbitrary base change in the cited theorem.

source.place: Section 2, Corollary 2.6 and smooth disjoint-section case; agent assembly from the cited universal-curve statement and the specified 2-cartesian squares. Local PDF WANTED.

proof.text: Conversely start with $(m_0,\beta)$ and put $\alpha_0=\beta$. Suppose $(m_r,\alpha_r)$ has been constructed. On $a_r(m_r)=X_r\times_{T_r}B$ choose the extra section $\sigma_{r+1}=\alpha_r^{-1}p_{r+1,B}$. This family is smooth, its previous sections map to $p_{1,B},\ldots,p_{r,B}$, and $\sigma_{r+1}$ is disjoint from them. Apply the cited universal-curve theorem to this family and section. It gives a stable $(r+1)$-pointed object with underlying curve unchanged, identified by $\alpha_r$ with $C_{r+1}=(C_B,p_{1,B},\ldots,p_{r+1,B})$; write $\delta_r:F_rC_{r+1}\xrightarrow{\sim}C_r$ for the canonical forgetting identification. Apply step 1 to $(m_r,C_{r+1},\delta_r^{-1}\alpha_r)$. It gives the unique $(m_{r+1},\alpha_{r+1})$ with $q_rm_{r+1}=m_r$ and $\delta_r F_r(\alpha_{r+1})\chi_r(m_{r+1})=\alpha_r$. Iterate for $r=0,\ldots,n-1$. This proves existence without needing to classify curves by coarse moduli points.

source.place: Section 2, Corollary 2.6 and smooth disjoint-section case; agent assembly from the cited universal-curve statement and the specified 2-cartesian squares. Local PDF WANTED.

proof.text: The forward recursion applied to the constructed inverse recovers every $\alpha_r$ by the compatibility equation in step 3 and every $m_r$ by $q_rm_{r+1}=m_r$; in particular it recovers $(m_0,\beta)$. Starting instead from a pointed pair, its truncations in step 2 already satisfy those same equations. At each stage step 1 gives only one possible pair over $(m_r,C_{r+1},\delta_r^{-1}\alpha_r)$, so induction shows the inverse construction recovers the original $(m_n,\alpha_n)$ exactly. Under the resulting identifications of underlying curves with $X_0\times_{T_0}B$, its $i$th marking is $\beta^{-1}p_{i,B}$, by the section formula in step 3. Distinct labels are retained throughout: changing $\alpha_n$ by a nonidentity automorphism cannot preserve its unpointed pair, since the two-sided inverse just proved would then recover two different pairs from the same input.

source.place: Section 2, Corollary 2.6 and smooth disjoint-section case; agent assembly from the cited universal-curve statement and the specified 2-cartesian squares. Local PDF WANTED.

proof.text: For a morphism $u:B'\to B$ of $F$-schemes, precomposition sends $m_r$ to $m_ru$, and pulling back $\alpha_r$, $\delta_r$ and the specified $\chi_r$ pulls back the recursion equation of step 2, using the canonical associativity identifications of fibre products from the definition. The contraction/stabilization comparisons commute with this pullback by the cited theorem. Moreover $u^*(\alpha_r^{-1}p_{r+1,B})=(u^*\alpha_r)^{-1}p_{r+1,B'}$. Hence the pulled-back inverse candidate satisfies precisely the equation defining the unique pair of step 1 over $B'$, and is that inverse. Both maps therefore commute with every pullback, including nonreduced or empty bases. When $n=0$ both are identities. No permutation or automorphism quotient occurs in any construction.
